content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to find suitable templates for disconnections.

The target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

It has a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl sulfone (para to methyl). The sulfonamide attaches to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamoyl anilide) attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-p-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

Potential disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline. So precursor: p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride (or p-tolyl-sulfonic acid) and the aniline bearing the cinnamoyl amide (i.e., 4-(cinnamoylamino)phenyl). Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the p-tolyl ring (the sulfonyl attached to p-tolyl). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the other phenyl ring (the one bearing the cinnamoyl). So we can disconnect S-N to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and the aniline (the other phenyl) with the amide side chain.

2) Disconnection of amide: break C-N to give aniline (the same phenyl) and an acid (cinnamic acid). So we could have aniline (the same phenyl) and cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative). But note the aniline is also part of sulfonamide; after step 1 we have the aniline with sulfonyl attached? Actually after step 1 we have the aniline bearing the sulfonyl group (since the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to that phenyl). So the amide disconnection would be on that same aniline (the nitrogen of amide is attached to the same aniline). So we could do a two-step route: first form amide via coupling of aniline (with sulfonyl) with cinnamic acid (or activated). Then form sulfonamide via reaction of sulfonyl chloride with that aniline (or maybe reverse order). Both steps are typical.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> (1) disconnect amide: gives intermediate A: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-aniline (i.e., p-tolyl-sulfonyl-4-aminophenyl) and cinnamic acid (or its derivative). Then (2) disconnect sulfonamide: gives p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride and 4-aminophenyl (aniline). However the aniline after step 1 is already the same as after step 2? Actually after step 2 we have the aniline (4-aminophenyl) which then undergoes sulfonylation to give sulfonamide intermediate A. Then step 1 amide formation attaches cinnamic acid to that aniline (now sulfonylated). So order: first sulfonylation, then amide coupling.

Thus retrosynthesis tree: target -> reaction1 (amide formation) -> precursor1 (sulfonylated aniline) + cinnamic acid. Then precursor1 -> reaction2 (sulfonylation) -> p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + 4-aminophenyl (aniline). Leaves: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride, 4-aminophenyl (aniline), cinnamic acid. All commercially available.

We need to find templates for sulfonyl chloride formation (sulfonylation of amine) and amide coupling (amidation of aniline with acid). Use search to find templates.

Search for amide formation: functional_groups_formed amide. Already got a template earlier (reaction_id 851565) but that seems to be for forming amide from acid and amine? The retro template shows O-C(=O)-CH2-... etc. Might be for amide formation via coupling of acid chloride? Not sure.

Better to search for "amide formation" with functional_groups_formed amide and maybe bonds_formed "C-N". But bonds format is numeric. Could ignore.

Let's just retrieve template by ID from earlier result? We have template hash but not ID. The result includes reaction_id 851565. We can get_template.
